plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do or believe, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks losses if you win at a price above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since values are private and independent, the optimal strategy is straightforward truth-telling: bid exactly my value of $25, ensuring maximum expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy: if you bid higher than your value, you risk winning at a price above your value (loss); if you bid lower, you risk losing an item you'd have profited from. This holds regardless of the other bidders' strategies, since the payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (unless you're the winner). Therefore, I will bid exactly my value, $18, to guarantee optimal expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' behavior. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no benefit to overbidding or underbidding - both introduce risk of either losing value I could have captured or overpaying. Truthful bidding is optimal here: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price exceeding my value; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $31.
